newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates edge lower.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates edge lower.

text.p: Dutch call money edged lower on Monday, after peaking for two successive days last week, but dealers said trade was very slow ahead of Friday's expiry of the three-month secured loans pact.
Call money was trading at 3.00 percent bid, although some business was done at levels somewhat higher, dealers said.

Call money rates started to rise rapidly last week and dealers said this could have been caused by money market participants who have already used up their quota under the secured loans pact ahead of Friday's expiry.
Call money was bid at 3.12 to 3.25 percent last week while other rates were unchanged for several days in a row.
"Hopefully the market will liven up again when the central bank sets a new quota on Friday," a dealer said.
Dealers expect the rate for the new special advances pact to be set at 1400 GMT today to be unchanged at 2.50 percent.
The guilder was trading this morning near previous levels at 112.16 per 100 marks versus 112.15 on Friday.
